newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: BRAZILIAN JARDEL SCORES TWICE IN PORTO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: BRAZILIAN JARDEL SCORES TWICE IN PORTO VICTORY.

text.p: Brazilian striker Mario Jardel scored twice on Saturday to help Porto, the reigning champions, to a 3-1 home win over Guimaraes in the Portuguese soccer championship.
Porto, the only unbeaten team, led the table with 38 points, with Benfica, who beat Leca 5-1 away on Friday, in second place five points behind.
The two old rivals meet next Saturday in a showcase match that Benfica cannot afford to lose if the club is to retain any hopes of the championship.
Jardel, the league's top scorer with 12 goals, scored his first in the eighth minute with a shot from outside the penalty area after a long pass from defender Fernando Mendes.
He got his second in the 31st minute with a shot inside the box after a corner by Serbian winger Ljubimko Drulovic.

Porto captain Jorge Costa, returning after an absence of six weeks because of a nose injury, scored the third in the 57th minute. Costa, a defender, shot the ball into the net in a goalmouth scramble after a free kick by midfielder Jose Barroso.
Striker Ricardo Lopes netted the consolation goal for Guimaraes in the 73rd minute.
Benfica's newly-signed Swedish striker, Martin Pringle, scored his first two goals in the win against Leca.
Benfica, playing their best soccer of the season in the opinion of sports commentators, completed the rout with goals by Osmar Donizete, Joao Pinto and Pedro Henriques.
Brazilian midfielder Alexandre Amaral and Dutch midfielder Glenn Helder made their debuts for Benfica.
